claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is initially in a high-temperature BCC state.
Phase stability in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is governed primarily by the composition-dependent Gibbs free-energy difference between BCC and FCC.
A more negative ΔGbcc-fcc drives transformation from BCC toward FCC during cooling.
Cooling-rate-dependent kinetic barriers can arrest the BCC-to-FCC transformation.
Slow cooling permits behavior closer to equilibrium than rapid quenching.
Rapid quenching limits transformation kinetics.
The relevant CALPHAD-based ΔGbcc-fcc calculations are reliable above approximately 0 °C.
The phase transition proceeds through nucleation and growth of FCC from a metastable BCC background.
Negative ΔGbcc-fcc supplies the thermodynamic driving force for FCC formation.
Slow cooling provides sufficient atomic mobility for FCC to nucleate and grow according to the thermodynamic prediction.
Rapid quenching preserves BCC by kinetically inhibiting transformation.
Slow-cooled samples will contain a measurable FCC phase fraction.
Rapidly quenched samples will remain predominantly BCC.
A phase-fraction difference between slow-cooled and quenched samples would directly demonstrate thermodynamic control of phase stability.
A standard quenching protocol can serve as a control that preserves the high-temperature BCC state without significant FCC nucleation.
Phase stability and transformation rate can correspond to thermodynamic phase stability as composition and temperature vary in multicomponent alloys.
Phase-stabilizing additives, severe deformation, or oxidation may alter the intrinsic transformation kinetics.
Compositional inhomogeneity and local strain may affect the quantitative transformation rate independently of ΔGbcc-fcc.
The controlled test compares initially BCC samples subjected to slow cooling with composition-matched samples subjected to rapid quenching.
Failure to observe a statistically significant FCC-fraction increase after slow cooling, despite a calculated negative ΔGbcc-fcc, would falsify the proposed primary control by ΔGbcc-fcc.
